questions.question: What is theoretical probability based on?
choices: A mathematical model of possible outcomes
Only observed trial counts
The largest result in a sample
The average of all numerical outcomes

questions.question: What is experimental probability based on?
choices: Only a symmetry assumption
The order of answer choices
The maximum possible outcome
Observed outcomes from trials

questions.question: A spinner lands on blue in 18 of 60 trials. What is the experimental probability of blue?
A fair six-sided die is rolled. What is the theoretical probability of a result greater than 4?
Which formula calculates experimental probability?
choices: Observed successes divided by total trials
Total trials divided by observed successes
Observed successes minus total trials
Observed failures divided by observed successes

questions.question: A fair coin lands heads 7 times in 10 tosses. What remains its theoretical probability of heads on the next toss?
What does a relative frequency describe?
choices: The total number of possible outcomes
The difference between successes and failures
The fraction of trials producing an outcome
The order in which outcomes occurred

questions.question: Why might a fair coin's experimental probability differ from 1/2 in a short trial?
choices: A fair coin must alternate heads and tails
Random variation affects observed results
The probability changes after every toss
A fair coin cannot produce repeated heads

questions.question: What generally happens to relative frequency over many independent trials under a fixed probability model?
choices: It tends to approach the model's probability
It must equal the model's probability after every trial
It steadily increases toward 1
It becomes independent of the model

questions.question: A die shows a 6 in 40 of 200 rolls. What is the experimental probability of rolling 6?
A spinner has four equal sectors, one red. What is its theoretical probability of red?
Why does a simulation of 100 fair die rolls not have to produce exactly 50 even results?
choices: The even numbers are less likely
Expected proportions are not guarantees for a finite sample
Fair dice require unequal frequencies
Simulations cannot represent dice

questions.question: An event with probability 0.2 is repeated independently 150 times. What is the expected number of occurrences?
What would repeated large discrepancies between observed and predicted frequencies suggest?
choices: The theoretical probability must always be zero
Randomness has stopped working
Every individual trial was recorded incorrectly
The model or trial procedure deserves investigation

questions.question: A simulation uses digits 0–9 equally often in the long run. Which rule models an event with probability 0.3?
choices: Count only digit 3 as success
Count digits 0 through 3 as success
Count digits 0, 1, and 2 as success
Count digits 3 through 9 as success

questions.question: A free-throw shooter makes 36 of 50 attempts. Using that rate, how many makes are predicted in 200 similar attempts?
A fair coin has landed tails five times in a row. What is the probability of tails on the next independent toss?
Two classes test the same fair spinner. One runs 20 trials and the other 2000. Which generally gives a more stable estimate of its probabilities?
choices: The class with 20 trials
The class whose first trial is blue
Both must give exactly the same estimate
The class with 2000 trials

questions.question: A bag's colors are unknown. In 100 draws with replacement and remixing, 62 are red. What is a reasonable estimated probability of red?
A simulation predicts a 0.4 probability of rain on a day. Which statement is justified?
choices: It must rain for exactly 40% of that day
Rain is possible, but neither rain nor no rain is guaranteed
It must rain on every fourth day
It cannot rain on two consecutive days
